rendered:
Yes. The paper reports both LODs for only P. aeruginosa and L. monocytogenes, and CD is lower for both. It states that CD consistently achieved lower limit of detection (LOD) than UV–vis[1]. The gap is much bigger for P. aeruginosa. The differences below are my own calculations from the reported values (OD600 units).

- P. aeruginosa: CD 0.0034[2] vs UV–vis 0.0066[3]. The CD LOD is lower by 0.0032[4], which is about 48%[5] below the UV–vis value. Put another way, the UV–vis LOD is roughly 1.9[6] times the CD LOD.
- L. monocytogenes: CD 0.0123[7] vs UV–vis 0.0125[8]. The CD LOD is lower by only 0.0002[9], about 1.6%[10], so the methods are nearly the same here.

CD comes out ahead in both comparisons, but the margin varies a lot between the strains.
